title: Balfour Declaration
summary: On 2 November 1917 British foreign secretary Arthur Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild, of the British Zionist Federation, that the government favoured a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine, provided the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities were protected. The letter did not explicitly promise a state. One encyclopedia says it gave the Zionist movement legitimacy and that, for the Arabs of Palestine, it came to symbolize British abandonment of Arab independence goals.

where.historical_name: London, capital of the United Kingdom

importance.justification: It was a British government statement on Palestine that shaped later Zionist and Arab relations with Britain.

perspectives.account: Official recognition by a major power lent legitimacy to the movement; Zionists read the letter expansively, expecting unlimited Jewish immigration.
For the Arabs of Palestine the declaration came to symbolize British abandonment of Arab independence goals; cooperation between Arabs and Zionists ended in 1919.
